construct: Beta-1 adrenergic stimulation raises cAMP and activates PKA. PKA phosphorylates phospholamban, relieving its inhibitory effect on SERCA2a. Faster sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium reuptake accelerates the decline in cytosolic calcium during diastole and increases lusitropy.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: The experiment isolates faster sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium sequestration: calcium entry and RyR2 release are clamped and troponin-I phosphorylation is prevented. Beta-1/PKA phosphorylation of phospholamban uniquely relieves SERCA2a inhibition.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Troponin I is a real PKA substrate that can accelerate relaxation by decreasing myofilament calcium sensitivity, but the stem explicitly prevents its phosphorylation and asks specifically about SR calcium sequestration.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: With entry, release, and troponin-I effects excluded, phospholamban is the single protein whose phosphorylation accelerates SERCA2a-mediated calcium uptake.
